newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey - U.S. economy still looks robust.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey - U.S. economy still looks robust.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Thursday said there have been some indications that the economy has moderated recently but it still appears strong.
"There are some signs of slowing but the pace of economic growth still looks quite robust," Lindsey told reporters following a hearing on consumer debt.
Asked whether the high level of resource utilization in the economy would lead to higher inflation, Lindsey responded that it was unclear.

Lindsey pointed out that the current levels of resource utilization are consistent with levels where inflation might be expected. However, he said it is something that will require careful monitoring.
On the question of whether wage rises lead to increases in inflation, Lindsey said that is "not necessarily" the case always.
On the one hand, the Fed governor said, "there is nothing wrong with higher wages that are accompanied by productivity gains."
Lindsey said it is possible for wages to rise without causing a pickup in inflation.
However, he said there is also the possibility that inflation would increase in such a case and he added that that was "the more normal circumstance."
Lindsey was also asked about a recent Brookings Institution study that warned of the dangers of aiming for zero inflation.

Concerning zero inflation, Lindsey said "a lot of the issue is a measurement issue." He noted that many economists believe that there is an upward bias to the Consumer Price Index and that Fed officials take that into account when considering the goal of price stability.
Questioned about recent criticisms of the Fed's management and spending practices, Lindsey responded "we should spend our resources as well as possible. We want to be helpful."
He noted, however, that a lot of the central bank's functions are mandated by law.
He said it would be worthwhile to consider whether the Fed should get out of certain businesses, but he said he was "agnostic" on that subject.
